title: Whole Numbers up to Millions: Place Value, Reading and Writing
seo_title: Whole Numbers up to Millions – Primary 5 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Count, read and write whole numbers up to millions in figures and in words; give the place value of digits; compare and order large numbers. (summary of the NERDC Primary 5 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 maths worksheets on whole numbers up to millions: place value, the value of a digit, numbers in figures and words, comparing and ordering. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Split big numbers into groups of three digits.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Group the digits in threes from the right: millions, thousands, units. 4,382,105 = 4 million, 382 thousand, 105.
  • The value of a digit = the digit × its place. In 4,382,105 the 8 is worth 80,000.
  • To compare, first count the digits. If they have the same number of digits, compare from the left.

Examples

Example

Value of 3 in 6,305,218

3 is in the hundred thousands place

Answer: 300,000

Example

Write 2,040,600 in words

2 million, 40 thousand, 600

Answer: two million, forty thousand, six hundred

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading the comma as a decimal pointThe commas only group the digits; 2,040,600 is a whole number.
Forgetting zerosTwo million and forty thousand is 2,040,000, not 2,40,000.
Comparing from the rightAlways compare from the biggest place.

faq.q: How many zeros are in one million?

faq.a: Populations of states and cities, money in a bank and distances in space.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 2 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 2 hundred thousands = 200,000. The digit is 2, but its value is 200,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 9 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 9 thousands = 9,000. The digit is 9, but its value is 9,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 1 is in the millions place, so it is worth 1 million = 1,000,000. The digit is 1, but its value is 1,000,000.

items.q: In 1,438,625, which digit is in the hundred thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions. In 1,438,625 the hundred thousands digit is 4, worth 400,000.

items.q: In 4,852,169, which digit is in the ten thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions. In 4,852,169 the ten thousands digit is 5, worth 50,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 6 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 6 ten thousands = 60,000. The digit is 6, but its value is 60,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 5 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 5 hundreds = 500. The digit is 5, but its value is 500.

items.q: Which number has a 5 in the hundred thousands place?
items.e: The hundred thousands place is the 6th digit from the right (the first digit after the millions). In 7,594,628 the 5 is there, so it is worth 500,000.
Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 3,000,000 + 400,000 + 7,000 + 20 = 3,407,020.
Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 6,000,000 + 50,000 + 300 = 6,050,300.

items.q: Which number is four million, sixty thousand and five?
items.e: Write each part in its group of three digits: four million → 4, sixty thousand → 060, then 005. Fill every empty place with 0: 4,060,005.

items.q: Which number is two million, three hundred and seven thousand and eighty?
items.e: Write each part in its group of three digits: two million → 2, three hundred and seven thousand → 307, then 080. Fill every empty place with 0: 2,307,080.

items.q: Which number is nine million, four thousand, three hundred?
items.e: Write each part in its group of three digits: nine million → 9, four thousand → 004, then 300. Fill every empty place with 0: 9,004,300.

items.q: In 3,606,000, how many times greater is the value of the first 6 than the value of the second 6?
items.e: The first 6 is worth 600,000. The second 6 is worth 6,000. 600,000 ÷ 6,000 = 100. Each place to the left is worth 10 times more, and the 6s are two places apart: 10 × 10 = 100. (594,000 is the difference, not how many times greater.)

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 2 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 2 hundred thousands = 200,000. The digit is 2, but its value is 200,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?

items.q: In 2,401,396, which digit is in the hundred thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions. In 2,401,396 the hundred thousands digit is 4, worth 400,000.

items.q: In 8,236,150, which digit is in the ten thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions. In 8,236,150 the ten thousands digit is 3, worth 30,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?

items.q: In 816,975, which digit is in the ten thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 816,975 the ten thousands digit is 1, worth 10,000.

items.q: In 385,601, which digit is in the hundred thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 385,601 the hundred thousands digit is 3, worth 300,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?

items.q: Which number has a 7 in the ten thousands place?
items.e: In a 6-digit number the ten thousands place is the 2nd digit from the left (5th from the right). In 873,245 the 7 is there, so it is worth 70,000.
Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 500,000 + 3,000 + 80 + 2 = 503,082.

items.q: What number is 60,000 + 700 + 4?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 60,000 + 700 + 4 = 60,704.

items.q: Which number is three hundred and four thousand and twenty?
items.e: Write the thousands part first: three hundred and four thousand → 304. Then the last three digits: twenty → 020. Fill every empty place with 0: 304,020.

items.q: Which number is seventy thousand, six hundred and five?
items.e: Write the thousands part first: seventy thousand → 70. Then the last three digits: six hundred and five → 605. Fill every empty place with 0: 70,605.

items.q: Which number is two hundred and fifty thousand and nine?
items.e: Write the thousands part first: two hundred and fifty thousand → 250. Then the last three digits: nine → 009. Fill every empty place with 0: 250,009.

items.q: In 330,000, how many times greater is the value of the first 3 than the value of the second 3?
items.e: The first 3 is worth 300,000. The second 3 is worth 30,000. 300,000 ÷ 30,000 = 10. Each place to the left is worth 10 times more. (270,000 is the difference, not how many times greater.)

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 4 thousands = 4,000. The digit is 4, but its value is 4,000.

items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 685,973 the ten thousands digit is 8, worth 80,000.

items.q: In 805,167, which digit is in the hundred thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 805,167 the hundred thousands digit is 8, worth 800,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 4 ten thousands = 40,000. The digit is 4, but its value is 40,000.

items.q: What is 10,000 more than 245,318?
items.e: Only the ten thousands digit changes: 4 → 5. The other digits stay the same. 245,318 + 10,000 = 255,318.

items.q: What is 100,000 less than 708,452?
items.e: Only the hundred thousands digit changes: 7 → 6. The other digits stay the same. 708,452 − 100,000 = 608,452.

items.q: Count in 100s: 46,800, 46,900, 47,000, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 more than the one before. 47,000 + 100 = 47,100. Only the hundreds digit changes.
Each number is 1,000 more than the one before. 130,500 + 1,000 = 131,500. Only the thousands digit changes.
Each number is 10,000 more than the one before. 57,450 + 10,000 = 67,450. Only the ten thousands digit changes.
Each number is 100,000 more than the one before. 350,000 + 100,000 = 450,000. Only the hundred thousands digit changes.
Only the ten thousands digit changes: 3, 4, 5, 6. So each number is 10,000 more than the one before.
Only the thousands digit changes and it gets smaller: 8, 7, 6, 5. So the rule is take away 1,000.

items.q: 10,000 more than a number is 482,150. What is the number?
items.e: Work backwards. If 10,000 more than the number is 482,150, the number is 10,000 less than 482,150: 472,150.

items.q: 100,000 less than a number is 360,400. What is the number?
items.e: Work backwards. If 100,000 less than the number is 360,400, the number is 100,000 more than 360,400: 460,400.

items.q: Which number is four million?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: four million → 4; no thousands → 000; nothing more → 000. So the number is 4,000,000. Four million has six zeros after the 4.

items.q: Which number is six million, two hundred thousand?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: six million → 6; two hundred thousand → 200; nothing more → 000. So the number is 6,200,000.

items.q: Which number is two million, forty thousand and six?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: two million → 2; forty thousand → 040; six → 006. So the number is 2,040,006. 246 and 2 400 006 leave out zeros that hold empty places.

items.q: Which number is 4 million and 25 thousand?
items.e: 4 million = 4 000 000. 25 thousand = 25 000. 4 000 000 + 25 000 = 4 025 000. The thousands group needs three digits: 025.

items.q: Which number is five million, three hundred and eight thousand?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: five million → 5; three hundred and eight thousand → 308; nothing more → 000. So the number is 5,308,000.

items.q: Which number is seven million and twenty-five?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: seven million → 7; no thousands → 000; twenty-five → 025. So the number is 7,000,025.

items.q: Which number is one million, nine hundred and fifty thousand?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: one million → 1; nine hundred and fifty thousand → 950; nothing more → 000. So the number is 1,950,000.

items.q: Which number is ten million?
items.e: Ten million = 10 × 1 000 000 = 10 000 000. Ten million is 10 millions: a 1, a 0 and six more zeros.

items.q: Which number is 3 millions, 2 ten thousands and 8 units?
items.e: 3,000,000 + 20 000 + 8 = 3 020 008. Write 0 for the hundred thousands, thousands, hundreds and tens.

items.q: Which number is three million, seventy thousand, four hundred and one?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: three million → 3; seventy thousand → 070; four hundred and one → 401. So the number is 3,070,401.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 9 ten thousands is more than 8 ten thousands. So 6,098,450 > 6,089,450.

items.q: What is 10,000 more than 4,995,300?
items.e: Add 1 to the ten thousands digit: 9 ten thousands + 1 = 10 ten thousands. Exchange them for 1 hundred thousand, then 9 + 1 = 10 hundred thousands, so exchange again for 1 million. 4,995,300 + 10,000 = 5,005,300.

items.q: What is 100,000 less than 2,034,500?
items.e: There are 0 hundred thousands, so exchange 1 million for 10 hundred thousands. 10 − 1 = 9 hundred thousands and 1 million is left. 2,034,500 − 100,000 = 1,934,500.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundred thousands place: 4 hundred thousands is more than 1 hundred thousand. So 7,451,936 > 7,154,639. 7,451,936 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the thousands place: 8 thousands is more than 4 thousands. So 5,628,493 > 5,624,983. 5,624,983 is the smallest.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 there are 10 equal jumps, so each mark is 100,000, not 10,000. The arrow is 7 marks after 2,000,000: 2,000,000 + 700,000 = 2,700,000.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 5,000,000 to 6,000,000 there are 10 equal jumps, so each mark is 100,000, not 10,000. The arrow is 4 marks after 5,000,000: 5,000,000 + 400,000 = 5,400,000.

items.q: Put 2,435,167, 2,437,561, 2,435,671 in order from smallest to greatest.
Put 3,892,574, 3,298,475, 3,897,425 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 3,298,475 < 3,892,574 (hundred thousands: 2 < 8). 3,892,574 < 3,897,425 (thousands: 2 < 7). So the order is 3,298,475, 3,892,574, 3,897,425.

items.q: Put 6,598,172, 6,951,872, 6,597,812 in order from greatest to smallest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 6,597,812 < 6,598,172 (thousands: 7 < 8). 6,598,172 < 6,951,872 (hundred thousands: 5 < 9). So the order is 6,951,872, 6,598,172, 6,597,812.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 1,000,000 there are 10 equal jumps, so each mark is 100,000. The arrow is 7 marks after 0: 700,000.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 300,000 to 400,000 there are 10 equal jumps, so each mark is 10,000, not 1,000. The arrow is 6 marks after 300,000: 300,000 + 60,000 = 360,000.

items.q: Which number is between 450,000 and 460,000?
items.e: Numbers between 450,000 and 460,000 have 4 hundred thousands and 5 ten thousands. 455,800 fits. 45,980 has only 5 digits, so it is much smaller.

items.q: Put 824,137, 842,317, 812,437 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 812,437 < 824,137 (ten thousands: 1 < 2). 824,137 < 842,317 (ten thousands: 2 < 4). So the order is 812,437, 824,137, 842,317.

items.q: Put 963,178, 967,318, 961,738 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 961,738 < 963,178 (thousands: 1 < 3). 963,178 < 967,318 (thousands: 3 < 7). So the order is 961,738, 963,178, 967,318.

items.q: Put 652,734, 625,437, 652,347 in order from greatest to smallest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 625,437 < 652,347 (ten thousands: 2 < 5). 652,347 < 652,734 (hundreds: 3 < 7). So the order is 652,734, 652,347, 625,437.

items.q: 6☐4,500 > 674,000. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The hundred thousands are the same (6). Compare the ten thousands: the box must be 7 or more. 4, 5 and 6 are too small. 684,500 > 674,000.

items.q: 3☐,850 < 34,100. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The ten thousands are the same (3). Compare the thousands: the box must be 4 or less. If it is 4, compare the hundreds: 8 > 1, so 34,850 would be too big. 33,850 < 34,100.

items.q: Use each of the digits 4, 0, 7, 2, 9 and 5 once. What is the greatest 6-digit number you can make?
items.e: Put the biggest digit in the hundred thousands place, then the next biggest, and so on: 9, 7, 5, 4, 2, 0. The greatest number is 975,420.

items.q: Use each of the digits 3, 0, 8, 1, 6 and 5 once. What is the smallest 6-digit number you can make?
items.e: Put the smallest digits first, but a 6-digit number cannot start with 0. Start with 1, then 0, then 3, 5, 6, 8: 103,568. (013,568 is really 13,568, a 5-digit number.)

items.q: A bus company counted one million, six hundred and five thousand and forty rides paid with EZ-Link cards in one week. Write the number in numerals.
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: one million → 1; six hundred and five thousand → 605; forty → 040. So the number is 1,605,040.

items.q: Library A has 1,245,000 books. Library B has 1,254,000 books. Which library has more books?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 5 ten thousands is more than 4 ten thousands. So 1,254,000 > 1,245,000. Library B has more books.

items.q: Kayode’s mystery number has 5 millions, 0 hundred thousands, 3 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 9 hundreds, 0 tens and 4 units. What is his number?
items.e: Write one digit for each place, with 0 for the empty places: 5, 0, 3, 0, 9, 0, 4. That is 5 030 904.

items.q: Yusuf reads a number aloud: “seven million, seven thousand and seventy”. Which number should he write?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: seven million → 7; seven thousand → 007; seventy → 070. So the number is 7,007,070.

items.q: City P has 1,085,000 people, City Q has 1,058,000 people and City R has 1,580,000 people. Which list goes from the most people to the fewest?
c: City R, City P, City Q
City Q, City P, City R
City P, City Q, City R
City R, City Q, City P
items.e: All have 1 million. Hundred thousands: 5 > 0, so City R has the most. City P and City Q both have 0 hundred thousands. Ten thousands: 8 > 5, so City P has more than City Q. Order: City R, City P, City Q.

items.q: A factory makes 45,000 drink cans a day. How many cans does it make in 100 days?
items.e: 45,000 × 100: multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left. 45 000 × 100 = 4 500 000. (450 000 is × 10 and 45 000 000 is × 1,000.)

items.q: Ruth makes the greatest 7-digit number that has 7 different digits. What is her number?
items.e: Use the greatest digits, each only once, from the millions place down: 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3. Her number is 9 876 543. (9 999 999 uses the same digit 7 times.)

items.q: A theme park had 2,500,000 visitors last year. This year it had 400,000 more visitors than last year. How many visitors did it have this year?
items.e: This year’s bar is last year’s bar plus 400 000. 2 500 000 + 400 000 = 2 900 000. (2 100 000 subtracts instead of adding.)

items.q: Book Fair A had 1,350,000 visitors. Book Fair B had 2,100,000 visitors. How many more visitors did Fair B have than Fair A?
items.e: The difference is the part marked ?. 2 100 000 − 1 350 000 = 750 000. Rename 1 million as 10 hundred thousands first. (1 250 000 takes the smaller digit from the bigger one in each place.)

items.q: A museum had 1,800,000 visitors in two years. In the 2nd year it had twice as many visitors as in the 1st year. How many visitors did it have in the 1st year?
items.e: 1st year = 1 unit, 2nd year = 2 units. 3 units = 1 800 000. 1 unit = 1 800 000 ÷ 3 = 600 000. (900 000 splits the total into 2 parts, and 1 200 000 is the 2nd year.)

items.q: A theme park had 1,995,800 visitors last year. This year it had 10,000 more. How many visitors did it have this year?
items.e: Add 1 to the ten thousands digit: 9 + 1 = 10, so exchange for 1 hundred thousand. Then 9 + 1 = 10 hundred thousands, so exchange for 1 million. 1,995,800 + 10,000 = 2,005,800.

items.q: At midnight the temperature was −8 °C. By 9 am it had risen by 5 degrees. What was the temperature at 9 am?
items.e: Risen means count up. From −8 °C count up 5: −7, −6, −5, −4, −3. It is still below 0: −3 °C.

items.q: At the 2,021 census, Leeds had a population of 811,953. What is this rounded to the nearest 10,000?
items.e: 811,953 is between 810,000 and 820,000. Look at the thousands digit: 1. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 810,000 people.

items.q: A submarine is at −250 m (250 m below sea level). It rises 180 m. Where is it now?
items.e: Rising means count up. −250 + 180: it is still 70 m below sea level, so −70 m.

items.q: At 6 pm the temperature was 3 °C. During the night it fell by 9 degrees. What was the temperature then?
items.e: Fell means count down. Count down 3 to reach 0, then 6 more: −6 °C. (3 − 9 is not 6.)

items.q: The population of a town, rounded to the nearest 10,000, is 250,000. What is the smallest the population could be?
items.e: Numbers from 245,000 to 254,999 round to 250,000. 244,999 would round down to 240,000, so the smallest is 245,000. (254,999 is the greatest.)

items.q: Samuel has the digit cards 7, 0, 3, 9, 1, 5 and 2. He uses each card once to make the smallest 7-digit number he can. What number does he make?
items.e: Put the smallest digits first, but a 7-digit number cannot start with 0. Start with 1, then 0, then 2, 3, 5, 7, 9: 1,023,579. (0,123,579 is really 123,579, a 6-digit number.)

items.q: A freezer is at −18 °C. A fridge is at 4 °C. How many degrees warmer is the fridge?
items.e: Count in two jumps through 0. From −18 °C to 0 °C is 18. From 0 °C to 4 °C is 4. 18 + 4 = 22 degrees. Do not work out 18 − 4.

items.q: The average distance from the Earth to the Moon is 384,400 km. What is this to the nearest 10,000 km?
items.e: 384,400 is between 380,000 and 390,000. Look at the thousands digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 380,000 km.

items.q: In a shopping centre, the ground floor is level 0 and the car park levels are −1 and −2. Uju takes the lift from level 3 down to level −2. How many levels does she go down?
items.e: From level 3 down to 0 is 3 levels. From 0 down to −2 is 2 levels. 3 + 2 = 5 levels.
